image_description: A high-angle, close-up shot of a Nile crocodile partially submerged in murky water. The view focuses on the dorsal surface of the head and upper back, highlighting the rough, armored texture of the scutes. The snout is visible at the bottom center, pointing downwards, while the body extends upwards into the water. A blurry, light-colored object (possibly a stick or tool) is visible in the top left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a point in a distinct V-shape, consistent with Crocodylus niloticus morphology rather than the U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the angle/position makes it impossible to see the teeth or the interlocking mechanism (specifically the 4th lower tooth notch).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye ridges are visible, the eyes themselves appear closed or obscured by the angle and water reflection; pupils and membranes cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Two distinct nostril openings are clearly visible at the very tip of the snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows heavy armor plating and extends out of frame, implying elongation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal surface displays a highly detailed, regular pattern of raised, bony scutes running longitudinally down the spine.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of muddy browns and greys, and the texture is visibly rough and granular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows only the dorsal (top) side of the crocodile; the belly is completely occluded by the body and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs are visible in the frame; the crocodile is submerged or positioned such that legs are hidden.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in this crop; only the head and upper torso are shown.
